sections.h2: Where is a deed recorded in Perry County, KY?
sections.html:
The County Clerk in Hazard takes every deed, mortgage and release on Perry County land, from an office at 481 Main Street, Suite 102. The contact block on the clerk's site gives 606-439-0557 and weekday hours of 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, while the county government directory lists 606-436-4614 for the office. Some older pages on the clerk's site show different opening times, so phone ahead.

The counter is optional. The clerk's land records page names four e-recording services: Indecomm, CSC, Simplifile and ePN. Attorneys, title agents and lenders can also subscribe to eCCLIX, the clerk's online index, and view recorded documents from their own desks.

sections.h2: What must a deed show before the Perry County Clerk accepts it?
sections.html:
A deed that leaves out a required item comes back unrecorded. Kentucky clerks, Pike County's among them, publish this checklist:

  • Seller and buyer names with mailing addresses, plus the legal description and source of title.
  • A preparation statement and a return mailing address.
  • An address where the tax bill for the transfer year may be sent (KRS 382.135).
  • A sworn, notarized consideration statement signed by both sides, and the grantor's notarized signature.

A gift deed instead states the estimated fair cash value. Easement-only utility deeds and corrective deeds between the same parties skip the consideration statement. If the house came through a will or intestacy, the personal representative files an affidavit with the clerk before closing the estate. A quit claim deed passes only what the grantor holds, with no title warranty.

sections.h2: How much does the Perry County Clerk charge to record documents?
sections.html:
The clerk posts a minimum for each document type. This selection covers what turns up most in a sale or an estate.

Minimum recording fees posted by the Perry County Clerk
DocumentMinimum fee
Deed$50
Deed of correction$46
Easement$50
Mortgage$80
Release of mortgage, full or partial$46
Power of attorney$50
Affidavit of descent$50
Will$47
Certificate of delinquency release$46

Pages beyond the fifth cost $3 each on most items, and a mortgage adds $3 only after page 30. Since the table shows minimums, a long document costs more.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax figured on a Perry County sale?
sections.html:
The grantor owes it. Under KRS 142.050 the tax is a half dollar per $500 of value, rounded up, so the county median owner-occupied value of $91,800 yields 184 units and $92.00. The clerk collects before recording, keeps 5% as a collection fee, and sends the balance to the county treasurer every quarter.

  • Exempt: transfers between spouses or former spouses in a divorce, foreclosures and deeds in lieu, partitions and tax-sale deeds.
  • Exempt: parent-and-child or grandparent-and-grandchild transfers for nominal consideration.
  • Gifts and nominal-price deeds are taxed on the estimated open-market price.

A clerk who records a taxable deed without collecting faces a $50 fine for each offense.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes and liens through the Perry County Clerk?
sections.html:
On April 15 the sheriff's unpaid bills become certificates of delinquency in the clerk's hands, recorded as liens against the parcels. Interest accrues monthly, commissions are added, and the county attorney sends written notice. Revenue schedules the clerk's sale between 90 and 135 days after the handover.

The Perry County clerk's site points to a delinquent tax application and says eligible owners can arrange a payment plan through the county attorney. If an outside buyer purchases a certificate, the fee table shows $30 to record the assignment and $46 to record the later release. A seller with an open certificate should pay it, get the release recorded, and hand proof to the title company before closing.

sections.h2: Can Perry County Clerk staff run a title search for me?
sections.html:
They cannot. The clerk's FAQ says deputies are prohibited from title searching, though they will help a visitor browse. Copy requests go in writing with a book and page, an instrument number, or enough detail (borrower, lender, loan amount) to find the paper without a search. The office keeps a list of attorneys, paralegals and abstractors who do insured title work.

The site also promotes DocAlert, a free service from its records software company that emails an owner when a deed or mortgage is filed under that name. A seller with a vacant or inherited house gets an early warning of any fraudulent filing.

sections.h2: What do sellers face in the Perry County housing market?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 26,555 residents for 2025 against 28,473 in the 2020 count. The county had 11,481 households in 2020, 29.5% of them one person living alone, and a median age of 42.0. QuickFacts adds 2.42 people per household, 70.4% owner-occupancy, median gross rent of $798, owner costs of $1,167 with a mortgage, and median household income of $42,181.

The county spans 343 square miles along the North and Middle Forks of the Kentucky River and borders Breathitt, Knott, Letcher, Harlan, Leslie, Clay and Owsley counties. Perry County Schools run Perry County Central High School and elementary schools named East Perry, Robinson, R.W. Combs, West Perry and Viper, along with Buck School. Hazard Independent Schools cover the city with Hazard High School, Hazard Middle School and Roy G. Eversole Elementary, and Hazard Christian Academy is the private option. Hazard Community and Technical College and the Hazard ARH Regional Medical Center are the best-known institutions.

Population history explains the vacancy numbers. Perry County grew from 11,255 residents in 1910 to 26,042 in 1920 and 42,186 in 1930, topping out at 47,828 in 1940. It then lost people in each count through 1970, when it held 26,259, rebounded to 33,763 in 1980, and has drifted down at every count since: 30,283 in 1990, 29,390 in 2000, 28,712 in 2010 and 28,473 in 2020. The 2020 census also found 13,213 housing units with 13.1% of them vacant, and a rental vacancy rate of 9.1%.

Buckhorn Lake State Resort Park, on the Middle Fork, is the county's best-known recreation area, and the county holds a Kentucky Trail Town designation. Hazard and Buckhorn are the two incorporated cities, with Combs, Diablock, Jeff and part of Vicco as census-designated places. A large share of Perry County's addresses sit in named hollows and creek communities such as Ary, Bulan, Busy, Chavies, Dwarf, Happy, Typo and Viper, so ask the clerk to confirm how a parcel is indexed before searching by street address.

faqs.q: What is the Perry County Clerk's address for deeds?
faqs.a: 481 Main Street, Suite 102, Hazard, KY 41701. The clerk's contact block shows weekday hours of 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

faqs.q: What is the clerk's fee for a Perry County deed?
faqs.a: Fifty dollars is the posted minimum, with $3 added per page beyond five. Transfer tax on the deed's stated value is separate.

faqs.q: Can closing documents be recorded electronically in Perry County?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk's land records page lists Indecomm, CSC, Simplifile and ePN as e-recording services.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Perry County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it as grantor, at 50 cents for each $500 of value. A $91,800 deed produces $92.00.

faqs.q: Can the Perry County Clerk look up the owner of a parcel for me?
faqs.a: Staff will point you to the records but cannot perform a title search. Requests for copies must be in writing with a book and page, instrument number or similar detail.
